clue.text: A guitarist's shot archer?

indicators.note: something shot is wrecked or ruined, so the letters before it are broken up and rearranged

parts.note: every letter of these words, the S of the possessive included

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a guitarist's attempt at something makes them a bowman.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that the archer is a sign of the zodiac rather than a person with a bow.
explanation.definitionFit: The constellation and zodiac sign is traditionally pictured as a centaur drawing a bow, hence known as the Archer.

clue.text: Part of a matrix shown by u-boat's speed

parts.note: a U-boat is a sub, and the possessive adds S
pace is rate of movement

explanation.surface: A grid of data is revealed by how fast a German submarine travels.
explanation.walkthrough: Matrix suggests a film or a grid of numbers, but the answer is a mathematical term from linear algebra.
explanation.definitionFit: In linear algebra a subspace is a smaller vector space, such as one spanned by columns of a matrix, contained within a larger one.

clue.text: Heavenly festival chief's entertaining tango

parts.note: CIC is commander-in-chief
T is tango in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: The organiser of a lovely festival lays on a tango for guests.
explanation.definitionFit: Galactic relates to the galaxy, so it concerns the heavens and celestial bodies in the sky.

clue.text: Support half of those people with force

indicators.note: only one half of the word for those people is kept, the front portion

parts.note: those people are THEM, and the first two of its four letters are kept

explanation.surface: Backing half of a group of people who use strength.
explanation.definitionFit: A rule or law with teeth has real power to compel obedience, so the word can mean effective force.

clue.text: Joiner's smooth in bar

parts.note: and is a conjunction, a word that joins
to iron is to smooth out creases

explanation.surface: A carpenter is planing something flat inside a pub.
explanation.walkthrough: Joiner suggests a carpenter, but it is a grammatical joining word; bar looks like a pub.
explanation.definitionFit: An andiron is a metal support, one of a pair of firedogs, made from a horizontal iron rod holding logs in a hearth.

clue.text: I reportedly see bird coming back with lettuce

parts.note: taken as written

parts.note: the letter C is pronounced like the verb see

indicators.note: coming back means the bird's name is read from its end to its start in this down entry

parts.note: a grebe is a diving waterbird

explanation.surface: Someone says they spot a bird returning with a salad leaf in its beak.
explanation.definitionFit: Iceberg is a common variety of crisp, pale lettuce with a tightly packed round head.

clue.text: One selling special beer to youth in Seychelles

indicators.note: in places the young person inside the letters for the island nation

parts.note: S is an abbreviation for special

a lad is a young man

explanation.walkthrough: SY is the Seychelles' code on car plates, split around the youth.
explanation.definitionFit: A saleslady is a woman employed to sell goods in a shop, so she is one selling.

clue.text: Piece of germanium

parts.note: letters three to five of the element's name

explanation.definitionFit: In chess and draughts each counter or figure is called a man, so a man is a playing piece.

clue.text: Side on a large keyboard

parts.note: Man U is Manchester United, a football team or side
taken as written

explanation.surface: Describing a panel on the side of a big piano or computer keyboard.
explanation.walkthrough: Side in crosswords often means a team; Man U is the popular short name of Manchester United.
explanation.definitionFit: On an organ each keyboard played by the hands is called a manual, as opposed to the pedals.

clue.text: Eats without lady and son

clue.text: Anger about Government's rubbish

parts.note: bile means bitterness or anger

clue.text: Department coming up with small houses

parts.note: D is an abbreviation for department

explanation.walkthrough: Small looks like it describes the houses, but it gives its abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Dwellings are places where people live, so the word is a general synonym for homes or residences.

clue.text: Drudge has wrap with heroin

parts.note: to pack is to wrap up goods
horse is slang for heroin

explanation.surface: A lowly worker carries a parcel containing drugs.
explanation.definitionFit: A packhorse literally carries loads, and figuratively it is a person who does tedious heavy work for others.

clue.text: Put on coach

second meaning: short for stagecoach, a horse-drawn carriage

clue.text: Bloody politician touring Borders

parts.note: Con is short for a Conservative
rims are edges or borders

explanation.definitionFit: Crimson is the deep red colour of blood, and the word also means stained with blood.

clue.text: Police equipment motormouth's split up

parts.note: the compound word is read as its two halves, each clued separately below

trap is slang for mouth, as in shut your trap

explanation.surface: A fast talker's gang has broken up, and the police take note.
explanation.walkthrough: Motormouth is one word in the surface, a non-stop talker; it is read as motor plus mouth.
explanation.definitionFit: A speed trap is a stretch of road where officers measure vehicles' velocity with radar to catch drivers breaking the limit.

clue.text: King George alas is dull in America

parts.note: GR is Georgius Rex, King George's royal cipher
ay is an old exclamation of regret, as in ay me

explanation.surface: A lament that the king is boring to Americans.
explanation.walkthrough: In America is part of the definition: the spelling with A is the US form of the colour.
explanation.definitionFit: Gray is the American spelling of the colourless shade between black and white, used figuratively for drab and lifeless.

clue.text: Unlikely offer from private nursing home is nonchalant

definitions.text: Unlikely offer from private nursing home
definitions.meaning: first meaning, read as two words: a promise of looking after residents at no charge, which a commercial home would never make

explanation.walkthrough: The first half is whimsical: split the answer and it becomes an advertising slogan no private care home would print.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone carefree has no worries, so the word describes a casually unconcerned, nonchalant manner.

clue.text: One may be slightly inclined to be Green

definitions.text: One may be slightly inclined to be Green

parts.words: One may be slightly inclined to be Green
parts.note: surface reading: a person who leans a little towards environmental politics
setter's reading: a gentle gradient for beginners, graded green on European mountains

explanation.walkthrough: The capital G suggests the Green Party, but green is the colour code for the easiest pistes at ski resorts.
explanation.definitionFit: Ski runs are graded by colour, and green marks the gentlest descents, so a green run is barely sloping.

clue.text: Maybe Goodman's means of seeing French town

definitions.meaning: first meaning: an optical glass, with a nod to Len Goodman, the ballroom judge, whose possessive sounds identical
second meaning: a town in northern France, near Lille

explanation.surface: Perhaps a celebrity judge's way of viewing a provincial town in France.
explanation.walkthrough: Len Goodman was head judge on the BBC dance show Strictly Come Dancing; his name plus 's spells the answer too.
explanation.definitionFit: A lens is a curved glass that focuses light, as in eyes, spectacles and cameras, enabling vision.

clue.text: Author's right to be more authoritarian

parts.note: Laurence Sterne wrote Tristram Shandy
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A writer claims the right to become stricter.
explanation.definitionFit: Stern means strict and severe, so the comparative describes someone imposing discipline more harshly.

clue.text: TV presenter briefly in Channel Island with bird

indicators.note: in places the shortened name inside the island's letters

parts.note: Sark is a small island in the English Channel

indicators.note: briefly means cut short, so the final letter of the name is dropped

parts.note: Jeremy Kyle hosted a daytime British talk show

explanation.surface: A television host spends a short holiday on a Channel Island, birdwatching.
explanation.walkthrough: Jeremy Kyle presented an ITV chat show; Sark is one of the Channel Islands off Normandy.
explanation.definitionFit: The skylark is a small brown songbird famous for singing while hovering high in the air.

clue.text: Boss promoting European involved in wrestling

indicators.note: involved in means caught up inside, so these letters go into the sport

parts.note: sumo is Japanese wrestling
PR, public relations, is promoting an image
E is the abbreviation for European

explanation.surface: A chief executive promotes a European in the wrestling world.
explanation.definitionFit: A supremo is a person in overall charge, an informal term for the head of an organisation.

clue.text: Guards touch up regimental officers' ladies initially

definitions.note: plural noun; the answer is a single collective noun for a group of guards

parts.note: to pat is to touch lightly, and to touch up is to fondle

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so just the opening letter of each word counts

parts.note: first letters of the three words

explanation.surface: Soldiers on duty grope the wives of the regiment's officers.
explanation.definitionFit: A patrol is a detachment of soldiers or guards sent out to watch over an area.

clue.text: Transfer back

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to move a worker temporarily to another post (stress on the ... syllable)

explanation.walkthrough: Transfer back looks like one phrase meaning return; split them into two separate verbs.
explanation.definitionFit: Employers second staff to other departments, and in meetings members second a proposal to support it.

clue.text: Welsh politician's objective to improve

parts.note: AM was Assembly Member, of the Welsh Assembly
an end is an aim or goal

explanation.surface: A Welsh politician's goal is to make things better.
explanation.definitionFit: To amend a law or text is to correct or alter it for the better.

clue.text: Scouts — opportunists using Republican for sex

indicators.note: using one thing for another means swapping it in where the other stood

parts.note: exploiters take advantage of opportunities
R is the abbreviation for Republican
it is slang for sex or sex appeal

explanation.walkthrough: IT is crossword shorthand for sex appeal; take it out of the opportunists and put R in.
explanation.definitionFit: Explorers are people who scout unknown territory, and Explorer Scouts are the senior section of the Scout movement.

clue.text: Elderly person keeps books to hand

indicators.note: keeps means holds within, so the elderly person surrounds the books

parts.note: OAP is an old-age pensioner
NT is the New Testament, a set of books of the Bible

explanation.surface: A pensioner holds onto library books so they are always handy.
explanation.walkthrough: OAP, old-age pensioner, is British shorthand for a retired person.
explanation.definitionFit: Something on tap, like beer from a barrel, is readily available whenever wanted.

clue.text: Ordering reconstruction around American border with Mexico

parts.note: taken as written
A is the abbreviation for American

explanation.walkthrough: Ordering looks like part of the surface's command, but it is the raw letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The Rio Grande is the river forming much of the frontier between Texas and Mexico.

clue.text: Doctor's operation involves part of the body

parts.note: runs across the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.definitionFit: The torso is the trunk of the human body, without the head and limbs.

clue.text: Knight leaves country boy

parts.note: a land is a country

clue.text: Point gun in Arms and the Man?

explanation.surface: Someone aims a firearm, with weapons and a soldier in view.

explanation.definitionFit: A period piece is a play or work set in, and evoking, a particular historical era, as Shaw's comedy is.
